They also want to sell some autographed baseballs. User plans to attend a stamp show next quarter but has not specified where. They are expanding their vinyl collection into international pressings, especially rare Japanese records, and are considering selling some vinyl for space. Resources discussed: Discogs, eBay sold listings, MusicStack, Reverb, local record stores, Record Collector’s Guild or Vinyl Collector’s Price Guide, Facebook groups, forums, and local classifieds. Advice emphasized checking condition, rarity, demand, catalog number, pressing, country, edition, and flaws; taking good photos; and using safe payment methods. For rare Japanese pressings, prior guidance included Discogs, Yahoo! Japan Auctions, Rakuten, Japanese record shops/communities, and specialist sellers.

User owns a Leica camera and other vintage cameras, is considering buying a new lens for the Leica, and may sell some cameras or accessories to make room. They plan to list the Leica on Fred Miranda and Rangefinder Forum. The latest camera-sale discussion was whether to include the original lens and accessories: a complete, functional, original kit can attract more buyers and command more than a body-only listing; verify authenticity/originality, document condition, flaws, and repairs, research sold/comparable pricing, take clear photos including serial numbers, and list every accessory. Damaged or non-original items may be better sold separately, with pricing reflecting actual incremental value. Leica and photography learning resources suggested include Leica’s official site, Leica forums, Reddit r/photography, Photography Stack Exchange, B&H, Digital Photography School, The Phoblographer, LensRentals, Ansel Adams’s *The Camera*, Rudolf Kingslake’s *The Lens*, Günter Osterloh’s *Leica: A History of the Legendary Camera*, and Leica-focused YouTube channels.

User recently acquired a 1943 Lincoln Wheat Cent with a copper planchet error and wants to learn more about it. Error-coin resources suggested: PCGS, NGC, CoinWeek, Error Coin Information, Fred Weinberg’s *The Error Coin Encyclopedia*, Bill Fivaz and J.T. Stanton’s *Cherrypickers’ Guide to Rare Die Varieties*, The Official Red Book, CoinTalk, Coin Community, Reddit r/coincollecting, and specialist dealers. Advice was to verify authenticity, understand the exact error and minting history, consult reputable dealers or grading services, and consider PCGS/NGC submission if appropriate.
